notes:
Context: large North American fintech. Primary challenge is massive indexing scale + tight per-query economics. Goal: move from hybrid ES + homegrown ANN to single managed runtime for production.

Top-level requirements (from CTO & head of search):
- Index target: 100M -> 1B vectors (phase 1 = 100–500M, phase 2 = 1B+)
- Ingest throughput: sustained 25k–50k vectors/sec during backfills; steady-state ~5k/sec
- Query profile: peak 1k–2k QPS, 95% read heavy; typical top-k=50 then rerank top-10 with expensive model
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms for full ANN+rerank pipeline (rerank model separate call)
detailed_requirements:
- Must support batching and cross-request KV/prefix caching to reduce token/regeneration cost for reranking stage.
- Need recommendations for quantization profiles (4-bit vs 8-bit) for candidate reranker to cut TCO.
- Automatic fallback: prefer cheaper embedding model for non-sensitive queries, fallback to higher-quality model for finance-sensitive endpoints.
- Support for hybrid search: BM25 prefilter + ANN, with consistent scoring for reranker.
- Index maintenance: rolling reindex that tolerates 10% downtime window, nearline compaction for PQ/OPQ.
- Ingest pipeline: native connector to Kafka and S3 bulk loader; metrics for ingestion lag and backpressure.
poC_acceptance_criteria:
1) Successfully ingest 100M vectors within 72 hours with sustained ingest >20k/sec for 8 hours.
2) Achieve p95 end-to-end (ANN + rerank) <= 120ms at 1k QPS.
3) Demonstrate cost model showing $ per query < $0.001 (target) at steady state.
4) Exportable audit logs + SSO integration validated.
sales_talking_points:
- Redwood Dedicated can provide predictable throughput and autoscaling for burst backfills.
- Redwood Optimize will supply batching/quantization recommendations to hit cost targets.
- Private deployment option available for data residency; installer subject to legal review.
- Can implement routing policy: cheap-embedding first, escalate to high-quality model for flagged docs.
recent_observations:
- Kilovectra is sensitive to unit economics: CFO asked for a 12-month TCO comparison vs current Milvus infra.
- They emphasized deterministic latency over lowest possible latency; prefer predictable p95 SLAs
- Engineering wants an API-compatible migration path (same endpoints) so product teams are not disrupted
- Concern that Redwood's on-prem installer maturity will be gating for procurement approval
